title: The Guardian
wiki_lead:
The Guardian is a British daily newspaper. It was founded in Manchester in 1821 as The Manchester Guardian and changed its name in 1959, followed by a move to London. Along with its sister paper, The Guardian Weekly, The Guardian is part of the Guardian Media Group, owned by the Scott Trust Limited. The trust was created in 1936 to "secure the financial and editorial independence of The Guardian in perpetuity and to safeguard the journalistic freedom and liberal values of The Guardian free from commercial or political interference". The trust was converted into a limited company in 2008, with a constitution written so as to maintain for The Guardian the same protections as were built into the structure of the Scott Trust by its creators. Profits are reinvested in its journalism rather than distributed to owners or shareholders. It is considered a newspaper of record in the UK.
The editor-in-chief Katharine Viner succeeded Alan Rusbridger in 2015. Since 2018, the paper's main newsprint sections have been published in tabloid format. In July 2021, the latest month for which figures are available, its print edition had a daily circulation of 105,134. The newspaper is available online; it lists UK, US (founded in 2011), Australian (founded in 2013), European, and International editions, and its website has sections for World, Europe, US, Americas, Asia, Australia, Middle East, Africa, New Zealand, Inequality, and Global development. It is published Monday–Saturday, though from 1993 to 2025 The Observer served as its Sunday sister paper.
The paper's readership is generally on the centre-left of British political opinion. In an Ipsos MORI research poll in September 2018 designed to interrogate the public's trust of specific titles online, The Guardian scored highest for digital-content news, with 84% of readers agreeing that they "trust what [they] see in it". A December 2018 report of a poll by the Publishers Audience Measurement Company stated that the paper's print edition was found to be the most trusted in the UK in the period from October 2017 to September 2018. It was also reported to be the most-read of the UK's "quality newsbrands", including digital editions; other "quality" brands included The Times, The Daily Telegraph, The Independent, and The i Paper. While The Guardian's print circulation is in decline, the report indicated that news from The Guardian, including that reported online, reaches more than 23 million UK adults each month.
Chief among the notable "scoops" obtained by the paper was the 2011 News International phone-hacking scandal—and in particular the hacking of the murdered English teenager Milly Dowler's telephone. The investigation led to the closure of the News of the World, the UK's best-selling Sunday newspaper and one of the highest-circulation newspapers in history. In June 2013, The Guardian broke news of the secret collection by the Obama administration of Verizon telephone records, and subsequently revealed the existence of the surveillance program PRISM after knowledge of it was leaked to the paper by the whistleblower and former National Security Agency contractor Edward Snowden. In 2016, The Guardian led an investigation into the Panama Papers, exposing then-prime minister David Cameron's links to offshore bank accounts. It has been named "newspaper of the year" four times at the annual British Press Awards, most recently in 2023.

grok_lead: The Guardian is a British daily newspaper founded on 5 May 1821 as The Manchester Guardian by John Edward Taylor, a Manchester cotton merchant, in response to the Peterloo Massacre and to advocate for liberal political reforms and free trade. Originally a weekly publication promoting the interests of industrialists and reformers, it transitioned to a daily format after the repeal of the Stamp Act in 1855 and relocated its editorial operations to London in 1961 while retaining its northern roots. Ownership resides with the Scott Trust Limited, established in 1936 to safeguard the newspaper's editorial independence and financial sustainability amid commercial pressures, insulating it from shareholder influences common in other media outlets. The publication is distinguished by its commitment to investigative journalism, having earned recognition for exposÃ©s on topics such as offshore finance and immigration scandals, including awards for investigation and journalist of the decade in 2022 for coverage of the Windrush scandal and related leaks. Its editorial stance aligns with centre-left positions, emphasizing social justice, environmentalism, and criticism of conservative policies, though media bias evaluators consistently rate it as left-leaning in story selection and framing, potentially reflecting broader institutional tendencies toward progressive viewpoints in mainstream journalism. Despite high factual reporting standards in many analyses, the newspaper has faced scrutiny for selective emphasis that may amplify certain narratives while downplaying others, contributing to perceptions of ideological slant over neutral empiricism. Under the Scott Trust's model, The Guardian operates with a reader-funded approach via voluntary contributions, aiming to prioritize journalistic integrity over advertising revenue, though this structure has not eliminated debates over objectivity in an era of polarized discourse. Its global influence extends through digital platforms and international editions, positioning it as a key voice in Anglo-American media, albeit one critiqued for aligning with establishment liberal consensus on issues like foreign policy and cultural matters.
